answer: An agent market serving a ferrous metal depot, a mesa solar farm, and an orchard allocates job invitations in proportion to escrowed stake, with deposits locked for 30 days. Splitting 1,000 tokens among a hundred fake identities earns the same total invitation probability as staking them under one identity. To gain more influence, an attacker must commit more capital and bear its month-long opportunity cost; creating names alone buys nothing.
